doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: North Philly and South Philly
summary: Ali and Grimes compare their sides of Market Street and name drummers from South Philly.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Henry, did you get to the Earle Theater at all? Is that something that you would have done?
Yeah I was. Yeah see it was in North Philly and I was in South Philly so I never got a chance in those places too much.
Well you know where the Earle was, right? It was right on 11th and Market.
Yeah. I’m familiar with it as, you know —

See Market Street divided North Philly and South Philly, and I lived on the north side of Market Street, Henry lived on the south side, which was, you know, like Jimmy Heath and all those guys from there were from down that way. And Tootie and all those guys. Tucker, that’s the drummer I was trying to tell you, Ronald Tucker. That’s the drummer I was trying to think about the other day, he was from down your way, right?
Yeah, Ronald Tucker, but I was thinking of another one, another guy. I know Ronald Tucker was one that was —
Yeah, Ronald, Ronald, Ronald, right, that’s right.
But this guy I’m trying to think of did the same thing. I haven’t seen him in years.
